thread:
maria (Support): we've got a couple customers reporting high tail latency and auth failures for EU users — looks like requests are landing in us-west. any ideas?
alan (Infra): seeing spikes in p50->p99 for eu-east tenants, yep a bunch of connections show x-region-served: us-west. weird.
sasha (Edge Eng): did the geoip tables change? last sync was overnight but should be fine. which ISPs/ASNs?
maria (Support): customer A (EU finance app) + customer B (e-com FR). both report 300ms -> 1.2s. they also saw 401s intermittently when requests routed to us-west.
jamie (SRE): 401s could be because tokens are region-scoped for private deployments? but these are hosted API customers, tokens should be global. can you paste a failing request/response header?
maria (Support): pasted sample curl from customer:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_*****" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.dev\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n< x-region-served: us-west\n< x-forwarded-for: 93.184.216.34\n< via: 1.1 varnish
```
alan (Infra): thanks. can you ask them to run: `dig +short api.redwood.dev A` and `dig +trace api.redwood.dev` and paste? suspect GeoIP->DNS anycast glue might be serving stale A records from some ISP caches.
sasha (Edge Eng): also check reply with `curl -I` to see cache headers. if TTL is low we should be ok, but some ISPs ignore low TTLs.
maria (Support): customer ran `dig`:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.dev
35.228.10.42\n$ dig +trace api.redwood.dev
; final answer: 35.228.10.42
```
alan (Infra): that IP is one of our us-west anycast pool addresses. hmm — the geoip service returns EU clients->eu anycast normally. looks like the resolver the ISP uses still has a stale mapping.
jamie (SRE): check our side: are healthcheck / routing rules correct? any recent canary that might have changed geoip mappings?
sasha (Edge Eng): no config changes on our side. I pulled geoip db version: 2026.03.10, synced last night. Routing policy still default prefer-region.
maria (Support): customer also says doing a VPN -> EU region fixes latency and 401s immediately.
alan (Infra): that confirms resolver path. workaround: set region param `?region=eu` for customer temporarily to force eu endpoints — but only for self-hosted or dedicated? our hosted REST supports `X-Region-Override` header for debugging, we can advise them to try `X-Region-Override: eu-west` for now.
jamie (SRE): long-term we need to purge affected DNS caches at the provider and escalate to upstream DNS/peers. which provider is serving this RRset? opsbot, pull dns provider info for api.redwood.dev.
OpsBot: DNS record for api.redwood.dev -> managed by dns-provider-1 (ns1.dns-p1.com). Current anycast pools: eu (35.197.8.10), us-west (35.228.10.42), apac (34.87.11.9). TTL=60. Last update: 2026-03-10T02:12:00Z.
maria (Support): customer notes they see stale us-west IP for multiple users across two ISPs in FR.
alan (Infra): TTL=60 so should've rolled quickly. but ISPs sometimes ignore low TTL. I'm going to open a ticket with dns-provider-1 to push immediate cache flush/notify peers. tagging @sasha @jamie.
sasha (Edge Eng): also let's add a diagnostic header showing resolver AS on our logs so we can map which upstream resolver returns which IP. jamie can you add to the quick SRE runbook?
jamie (SRE): on it. runbook note: 1) verify `dig +trace` 2) get client resolver IP from `x-forwarded-for`/tcp handshake 3) ask customer to `dig @<their-resolver> api.redwood.dev` 4) request provider cache purge 5) send temporary region override. I'll add command examples.
maria (Support): customer asked about billing — they saw higher token counts because latency caused retries and duplicate requests. is there a credit path?
alan (Infra): support can issue pro-rated credits for duplicated work due to routing bug. put details in the ticket. I'll annotate with affected time range.
sasha (Edge Eng): quick repro for infra: from our eu lab, `dig api.redwood.dev` returns eu IP. from a Paris office vpn exit it returns us-west. so cache is definitely at ISP resolver level.
maria (Support): filed support ticket #SUP-5421 with customer logs and asked them to try `X-Region-Override` header. they confirmed improved perf.
OpsBot: Incident created: INC-2026-043 - GeoIP/DNS cache causing cross-region routing for eu clients. Severity: high. Assigned: alan, sasha.
alan (Infra): update from provider: they see a minority of DNS peers still serving old anycast mapping due to a partial propagation issue. provider will push urgent purge and BGP re-advertise. ETA 25-40 minutes.
jamie (SRE): schedule: monitor for 1h after purge, look for drop in p99 and 401s. if not resolved escalate to upstream transit.
maria (Support): customers updated, most on-thread users reported improvement after provider purge at +32m. two small ISPs still sticky; we asked customers to file ticket with their ISP if they see caches ignoring TTL.
alan (Infra): follow-up task: add a fallback alignment check in routing logic so that when we do cross-region fallback we don't return region-scoped auth flows or cause token validation failures. created infra ticket INFRA-1197.
sasha (Edge Eng): also adding resolver AS logging and a dashboard to spot clusters of misrouted clients quickly.
maria (Support): closing loop with customers, issuing small usage credits. will keep INFRA-1197 linked to the support ticket. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
jamie (SRE): note for postmortem: root cause = ISP-level DNS caching ignoring low TTL + partial propagation at dns-provider. mitigations: faster provider purge workflow, resolver AS telemetry, region-override header doc, and routing fallback auth alignment.
OpsBot: INC-2026-043 status -> mitigated (2026-03-10T14:25:00Z).
